stages.name: Requirements
stages.entryQuestion: Before designing a photo-sharing service, what scope and scale assumptions would you clarify?
stages.objective: Agree on product behavior, measurable quality targets and the stated exercise workload.

completionCriteria.name: Functional scope
completionCriteria.guidance: Prioritize publish/read/follow and privacy; keep search, notifications and sophisticated recommendations optional.

completionCriteria.name: Quality targets
completionCriteria.guidance: Separate media durability, metadata freshness, private visibility and feed response latency.

completionCriteria.name: Capacity estimates
completionCriteria.guidance: Use the fictional baseline or state a justified alternative; derive average and peak rates and distinguish payload bytes from replication and indexes.

stages.name: High Level Design
stages.entryQuestion: Walk me through photo publication and a follower feed request.
stages.objective: Separate media bytes, post metadata, follower relationships and feed serving.

completionCriteria.name: Publication boundary
completionCriteria.guidance: Describe media upload and a post service that publishes only durable, accessible content.

completionCriteria.name: Feed boundary
completionCriteria.guidance: Separate follower lookup, candidate feed references and read serving; services may be colocated.

completionCriteria.name: Persistent storage
completionCriteria.guidance: Include durable post and relationship storage as well as object storage; caches are not the only copy.

completionCriteria.name: Optional extensions
completionCriteria.guidance: A search index or recommendation service is not required for a correct baseline.

stages.name: Core Flow
stages.entryQuestion: How does a new photo become visible in a follower feed without serving incomplete media?
stages.objective: Connect the media pipeline with a defensible feed-generation strategy.

completionCriteria.name: Media publication
completionCriteria.guidance: Upload to object storage, validate/checksum and create derivatives asynchronously; do not expose an unfinished asset.

completionCriteria.name: Fanout strategy
completionCriteria.guidance: Choose write fanout, read fanout or a hybrid, explaining the read/write tradeoff and high-degree authors.

completionCriteria.name: Feed ordering
completionCriteria.guidance: A reverse-chronological baseline is acceptable; use a stable tie-breaker and defend any ranking signal.

completionCriteria.name: Visibility filtering
completionCriteria.guidance: Apply current visibility/deletion rules when serving feed references rather than trusting stale fanout forever.

stages.name: Data Model
stages.entryQuestion: What schemas and indexes support posts, follows, comments and feed pagination?
stages.objective: Model social relationships and media references without storing blobs in relational rows.

completionCriteria.name: Post records
completionCriteria.guidance: Represent author, post ID, creation time, media manifest, visibility and deletion version.

completionCriteria.name: Relationship records
completionCriteria.guidance: Index follows by follower and author; make like/follow operations idempotent.

completionCriteria.name: Feed cursors
completionCriteria.guidance: Page by stable ordering key rather than deep offsets; handle deletion and repeated page requests.

completionCriteria.name: Engagement records
completionCriteria.guidance: Represent retried likes with a unique key and comments with post-scoped ordering, author access checks and deletion semantics.

stages.name: Reliability
stages.entryQuestion: How do failed media jobs, duplicate events and a privacy change affect published feeds?
stages.objective: Handle publication retries, stale feeds and access revocation safely.

completionCriteria.name: Retry correctness
completionCriteria.guidance: Use stable event IDs and idempotent derivative/fanout writes; reconcile metadata and objects after partial failure.

completionCriteria.name: Privacy and deletion
completionCriteria.guidance: Invalidate or filter private/deleted posts and use bounded authorized media links where needed.

completionCriteria.name: Degraded operation
completionCriteria.guidance: Bound worker backlogs and allow stale eligible feeds during a cache or ranking outage.

stages.name: Scaling
stages.entryQuestion: How would you size the feed, media pipeline and caches for the stated workload?
stages.objective: Budget media bytes separately from post and feed metadata.

completionCriteria.name: Media budget
completionCriteria.guidance: Derive about 2.10 TB/day of source photos and 62.91 TB in a 30-day cohort before copies, derivatives and video.

completionCriteria.name: Feed partitioning
completionCriteria.guidance: Partition by recipient or author as appropriate and isolate high-degree users from ordinary fanout.

completionCriteria.name: Cache and delivery
completionCriteria.guidance: Use bounded feed caches and CDN delivery of media; clients fetch media from the CDN/object path, not through an API-to-CDN RPC.

stages.name: Tradeoffs
stages.entryQuestion: Which tradeoffs matter most for feed freshness, privacy and media processing cost?
stages.objective: Explain the consequences of the chosen feed and storage mechanisms.

completionCriteria.name: Fanout tradeoff
completionCriteria.guidance: Compare write amplification with read aggregation and justify the high-degree author policy.

completionCriteria.name: Consistency tradeoff
completionCriteria.guidance: Allow eventual feed insertion but explain why private-content access and deletion require stronger checks.

completionCriteria.name: Product scope tradeoff
completionCriteria.guidance: Distinguish a valid chronological baseline from optional machine-learned ranking; discuss quality versus compute cost.
